top_story.headline: Rep. Dan Crenshaw still has no 2025 annual financial disclosure on file, 74 days past his final extension
top_story.dek: The Deadline Watch check flags the Texas Republican as the one sitting member with no CY2025 annual report on file after every extension has run out.
paragraphs: Rep. Dan Crenshaw (R-TX-2) filed an extension on 6/4/2026. His final extension date was 8/13/2026, and as of today no CY2025 annual financial disclosure appears under his name, 74 days later. He is the only sitting member the check found in that position.

The check compares every sitting member against the Clerk of the House index and Senate eFD. It is partial today: the Senate annual-report and Senate extension checks both failed with a parsing error, so the Senate side is unverified. A filing under an unexpected spelling of a name can also read as missing, so the result is a flag, not a confirmed non-filing.

Among the other deterministic extras, seven confirmed officials still have no posted certification of ethics-agreement compliance more than 30 days past deadline. The longest-running is Michelle White Bowman, Vice Chair for Supervision at the Federal Reserve System Board of Governors, whose certification was due 9/2/2025, 419 days ago. Today's OGE summary reported no new divestitures or terminations.

sections.headline: No new ethics divestitures or terminations reported

sections.headline: No new House or Senate disclosures in today's input; Senate eFD fetch failed
paragraphs: The input contained no new House or Senate financial disclosures filed since 2026-10-23 that earlier editions had not already reported, and no periodic transaction reports to parse. The Senate eFD fetch returned an error, so the Senate count reflects a failed check, not a confirmed absence of filings.

blocks.text: Tracking 483 Senate-confirmed officials with ethics agreements since Jan. 20, 2025. Deadlines are counted from the confirmation date on congress.gov plus the agreement's stated window (usually 90 days) -- OGE can grant extensions that aren't public, so treat each flag as a lead to confirm, not a finding. OGE posts certifications with a lag, so nothing inside 30 days of a deadline is flagged. A certification filed but not yet posted by OGE will read as missing: confirm with the agency before publishing.
